cases.title: 2022 Fed tightening
cases.context: FY2021 → FY2022 bank NII. Shock equals the change in annual-average effective federal funds rates, not the year-end target jump. Current bank sensitivities are scaled linearly; balance-sheet growth and deposit repricing remain confounders.
cases.cohort_rule: All configured companies with nonzero modeled exposure and complete annual pre/post data. Zero-exposure names and missing observations are disclosed as exclusions.

sources.label: FRED · daily effective federal funds rate

rows.name: JPMorgan Chase
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.source: JPMorgan 2025 10-K p.141 earnings-at-risk: +100 bps parallel shift +$2.1B (2024: +$2.3B; +200 bps +$3.7B) vs FY2025 NII $95,443M
assumptions.rationale: Low is half the +200 bp result (curvature); high is the 2024 sensitivity. JPM says non-USD sensitivities were insignificant.

assumptions.source: JPMorgan 2025 10-K p.141 earnings-at-risk: −100 bps parallel shift −$2.4B (−200 bps −$6.0B) vs FY2025 NII $95,443M
assumptions.rationale: High is half the −200 bp result; deposit-rate floors make larger cuts hurt more per bp.

rows.name: Bank of America
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.source: Bank of America 2025 10-K Table 45: +100 bps instantaneous parallel shift +$0.7B banking-book NII (2024: +$1.1B; +200 bps +$0.8B) vs FY2025 NII $60,096M
assumptions.rationale: Low is half the +200 bp result; high is the 2024 sensitivity.

assumptions.source: Bank of America 2025 10-K Table 45: −100 bps parallel shift −$2.0B (2024 −$2.3B; −200 bps −$4.9B) vs FY2025 NII $60,096M
assumptions.rationale: High is half the −200 bp result.

rows.name: Wells Fargo
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.source: Wells Fargo 2025 10-K Table 28: +100 bps parallel shift +$1.9B NII over 12 months (Dec 2024: +$1.3B) vs FY2025 NII $47,484M
assumptions.rationale: Low is the 2024 sensitivity. Excludes Markets trading NII.

assumptions.source: Wells Fargo 2025 10-K Table 28: −100 bps parallel shift −$2.3B (−200 bps −$5.3B) vs FY2025 NII $47,484M
assumptions.rationale: High is half the −200 bp result.

rows.name: Goldman Sachs
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.source: Goldman Sachs 2025 10-K earnings-at-risk: +100 bps parallel shift +$154M net revenues (+200 bps +$215M), expressed vs FY2025 NII $13,559M
assumptions.rationale: GS measures the effect on net revenues and preferred dividends; we express the same dollars per $ of NII so the bank_nii channel reproduces them. Low is half the +200 bp result.

assumptions.source: Goldman Sachs 2025 10-K earnings-at-risk: −100 bps parallel shift −$273M (−200 bps −$485M), vs FY2025 NII $13,559M
assumptions.rationale: Low is half the −200 bp result.

rows.name: Citigroup
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.source: Citigroup 2025 10-K interest rate exposure: +100 bps parallel shock, U.S. dollar component −$33M at Dec 31, 2025 (−$252M Sep 2025; all currencies +$1,369M) vs FY2025 NII $59,792M
assumptions.rationale: A Fed move shifts US dollar rates, so only the USD line applies; Citi's large positive sensitivity is in non-USD currencies. Low is the Sep 2025 USD figure.
Citi discloses only the +100 bp shock; we assume the USD effect is symmetric (−$33M), with a high case where deposit-rate floors make a cut hurt, as at the US peers.

rows.name: American Express
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.

assumptions.source: American Express 2025 10-K Table 22: +100 bps instantaneous parallel shock +$19M annual NII (Table 23, previous deposit-repricing assumptions: −$238M) vs FY2025 NII $17,364M
assumptions.rationale: Low uses Amex's previous deposit-repricing assumptions.

assumptions.source: American Express 2025 10-K Table 22: −100 bps shock −$11M annual NII (Table 23 previous assumptions: +$248M) vs FY2025 NII $17,364M
assumptions.rationale: Negative low means NII rises when rates fall under the previous assumptions.

sources.label: Federal Student Aid · enacted Pell award increase

rows.name: Grand Canyon Education
notes: Current configured exposures applied to old financials: retrospective replay with look-ahead exposure risk.
Observed growth includes organic demand, acquisitions, pricing and other policies.

assumptions.rationale: GCU's online and ground undergraduates include many Pell recipients. GCU took about 73% of revenue under the 90/10 rule from Title IV, per GCE's quarterly report as quoted by Higher Ed Dive (Feb 2020, stale). Pell is assumed to be a minority of that federal aid, with loans the majority.

Pell students at these schools usually also qualify for subsidised and unsubsidised Direct Loans with room under the limits, so many can borrow to replace lost grant aid; lower-income students are more loan-averse, so not all of it is replaced.

definition: Directional accuracy = 100 × same-sign modeled/observed company changes ÷ eligible company comparisons. Every eligible company-case has equal weight; zero observed changes are misses for a nonzero prediction. Missing inputs and zero modeled exposures are listed as exclusions.
limits: Retrospective current-model replays, not out-of-sample forecast validation or causal policy attribution. Six industry cases share the same TCJA episode; cases and company outcomes are correlated. Current exposures and restated historical statements can introduce look-ahead bias. No overall magnitude percentage is calculated across incompatible metrics.
